docs.title: VolumeMigrationSettings
docs.text:
VolumeMigrationSettings controls how volume migration and the post-migration realignment behave, not whether they happen. It is separate from VolumeAutoPlacementSettings because realignment applies to every volume move, whether it came from the auto-rebalancer, a manual migration, or a drain, so it cannot sit under the rebalancing policy that is only one of its three sources.

There is no switch here. Migration cannot be turned off: a drain, a rebalance, and a device replacement are all performed by moving volumes.

Appears in: - StorageClusterSpec

Example:

rebalancerImage: string
dataRealignment:
  interval: Duration
  minMoves: integer
Field Description Default Validation rebalancerImage string RebalancerImage is the container image the migration path-validation Joband the rebalancer's latency and baseline Jobs run. It must carrynvme-cli, and for rebalancing also fio and jq. Optional: {} dataRealignment DataRealignmentSettings DataRealignment tunes the post-migration realignment. Optional: {}

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Simplyblock is designed as a system for minimal manual intervention. However, once in a while, there may be issues that require some special treatment.

This section provides practical solutions for common issues encountered when deploying or operating simplyblock. Whether the problem is a deployment hiccup, a performance anomaly, a connectivity problem, or a configuration error, the step-by-step guidance below helps to diagnose and resolve it quickly. Use this guide to keep a simplyblock environment running smoothly and with confidence.

docs.title: FoundationDB Error
docs.text:
Symptom: FoundationDB error. All services that rely upon the FoundationDB key-value storage are offline or refuse to start.

  1. Ensure that IPv6 is disabled: Network Configuration
    sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1
  2. Ensure sufficient disk space on the root partition on all control plane nodes. Free disk space can be checked with df -h.
    1. If not enough free disk space is available, start by checking the Graylog, MongoDB, and Elasticsearch containers. If those consume most of the disk space, old indices (2-3) can be deleted.
    2. Increase the root partition size.
    3. If the root partition size cannot be increased, remove any data or service not relevant to the simplyblock control plane and run a docker system prune.
  3. Restart the Docker daemon: systemctl restart docker
  4. Reboot the node

docs.title: Graylog Service Is Unresponsive
docs.text:
Symptom: The Graylog service cannot be reached anymore or is unresponsive.

  1. Ensure enough free available memory
  2. If short on available memory, stop services non-relevant to the simplyblock control plane.
  3. If that doesn't help, reboot the host.

docs.title: Graylog Storage is Full
docs.text:
Symptom: The Graylog service cannot start or is unresponsive, and the storage disk is full.

  1. Identify the cause of the disk running full. Run the following commands to find the largest files on the Graylog disk. Find the largest files
    df -h
du -sh /var/lib/docker
du -sh /var/lib/docker/containers
du -sh /var/lib/docker/volumes
  2. Delete the old Graylog indices via the Graylog UI.
    • Go to System -> Indices
    • Select the index set
    • Adjust the Max Number of Indices to a lower number
  3. Reduce Docker disk usage by removing unused Docker volumes and images, as well as old containers. Remove old Docker entities
    docker volume prune -f
docker image prune -f
docker rm $(sudo docker ps -aq --filter "status=exited")
  4. Cleanup OpenSearch, Graylog, and MongoDB volume paths and restart the services. Cleaning up adjacent services
    # Scale services down
docker service update monitoring_graylog --replicas=0
docker service update monitoring_opensearch --replicas=0
docker service update monitoring_mongodb --replicas=0

# Remove old data
rm -rf /var/lib/docker/volumes/monitoring_graylog_data
rm -rf /var/lib/docker/volumes/monitoring_os_data
rm -rf /var/lib/docker/volumes/monitoring_mongodb_data

# Restart services
docker service update monitoring_mongodb --replicas=1
docker service update monitoring_opensearch --replicas=1
docker service update monitoring_graylog --replicas=1

docs.title: Kubernetes CSI
docs.text:
Simplyblock CSI integrates Kubernetes volume lifecycle operations (provision, attach, mount, unmount, delete) with the simplyblock storage backend.

Most CSI issues appear in one of three layers:

  • Kubernetes object lifecycle (PVC/PV/Pod events),
  • CSI controller/node plugin behavior,
  • node-level transport and NVMe subsystem state.

docs.title: High-Level CSI Driver Architecture
docs.text:
• Controller Plugin: Runs as a StatefulSet and manages volume provisioning and deletion.
  • Node Plugin: Runs as a DaemonSet and handles volume attachment, mounting, and unmounting.
  • Sidecars: Handle external provisioning (csi-provisioner), attaching (csi-attacher), and driver registration (csi-node-driver-registrar).

docs.title: Quick Component Health Checks
docs.text:
Start by validating CSI control-plane and node-plane pods:

List CSI pods
kubectl get pods -n <CSI_NAMESPACE> -o wide
Inspect CSI pod status and restart counts
kubectl get pods -n <CSI_NAMESPACE> \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount,NODE:.spec.nodeName

docs.title: Check Kubernetes Events First
docs.text:
Before deep host diagnostics, inspect object events for clear failure reasons:

Describe PVC
kubectl describe pvc <PVC_NAME> -n <WORKLOAD_NAMESPACE>
Describe pod using the PVC
kubectl describe pod <POD_NAME> -n <WORKLOAD_NAMESPACE>
View recent warning events
kubectl get events -A --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

docs.title: Trace a PVC End-to-End
docs.text:
Use this sequence to identify the right logs and host:

  1. Find pod(s) using the PVC.
  2. Resolve the node where the pod is scheduled.
  3. Locate the CSI node plugin pod on that node.
  4. Pull logs from the node plugin (and controller plugin if needed).
Find pods using the PVC
kubectl get pods -A -o \
jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}{"/"}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.volumes[*].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName}{"\n"}{end}' | \
grep <PVC_NAME>
Find node for the PVC-consuming pod
kubectl get pods -A -o \
jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}{"/"}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.nodeName}{"\t"}{.spec.volumes[*].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName}{"\n"}{end}' | \
grep <PVC_NAME>
Find CSI node plugin pod on target node
kubectl get pods -n <CSI_NAMESPACE> -o wide | grep <NODE_NAME>
Get CSI node plugin logs
kubectl logs -n <CSI_NAMESPACE> <CSI_NODE_POD> -c <DRIVER_CONTAINER>
Get CSI controller plugin logs
kubectl logs -n <CSI_NAMESPACE> <CSI_CONTROLLER_POD> -c <DRIVER_CONTAINER>

docs.title: Troubleshooting NVMe-Related Errors
docs.text: If errors indicate NVMe path issues (volume attachment failure, device not found, path loss), run the following checks on the affected worker node.

docs.title: 1) Ensure nvme-cli is installed
docs.text:
RHEL / Alma / RockyDebian / Ubuntu Install nvme-cli on RHEL-based systems
sudo dnf install -y nvme-cli
Install nvme-cli on Debian-based systems
sudo apt install -y nvme-cli

docs.title: 2) Verify nvme_tcp kernel module
docs.text:
Check NVMe/TCP kernel module
lsmod | grep nvme_tcp

If missing, load it:

Load NVMe/TCP kernel module
sudo modprobe nvme-tcp

Persist module loading across reboots:

Red Hat / Alma / RockyDebian / Ubuntu Persist nvme-tcp module (RHEL-based)
echo "nvme-tcp" | sudo tee -a /etc/modules-load.d/nvme-tcp.conf
Persist nvme-tcp module (Debian-based)
echo "nvme-tcp" | sudo tee -a /etc/modules

docs.title: 3) Check NVMe subsystem state
docs.text:
List NVMe subsystems
sudo nvme list-subsys

If expected subsystem is missing, reconnect manually:

Reconnect NVMe-oF subsystem
sudo nvme connect -t tcp \
    -n <NVME_SUBSYS_NAME> \
    -a <TARGET_IP> \
    -s <TARGET_PORT> \
    -l <CTRL_LOSS_TIMEOUT> \
    -c <RECONNECT_DELAY> \
    -i <NR_IO_QUEUES>

docs.title: 4) Collect node diagnostics
docs.text:
Collect NVMe-related kernel logs
sudo dmesg | grep -i nvme

docs.title: Common Failure Patterns
docs.text:
• timed out waiting for condition during mount: usually node-path or transport connectivity.
  • device not found after attach: often missing kernel module or failed subsystem connect.
  • repeated reconnect loops in logs: verify target IP/port, transport, and backend health.

docs.title: Symptom-to-Action Quick Index
docs.text:
• PVC stuck in Pending: check provisioning flow and CSI controller logs.
  • Pod stuck in ContainerCreating or mount timeout: trace PVC to node plugin logs.
  • Volume attach/mount failure with NVMe errors: run node-level NVMe diagnostics.
  • Intermittent I/O errors after attach: inspect kernel/NVMe subsystem state and reconnect path.

docs.title: Escalation Checklist
docs.text:
When escalating to support, collect:

  • CSI controller and node plugin logs around failure timestamp.
  • kubectl describe output for affected PVC and pod.
  • Node-level nvme list-subsys and dmesg output.
  • Affected resource identifiers: namespace, pod, PVC, PV, node, and approximate timestamps.

docs.title: Related References
docs.text:
• Install CSI Driver
  • Provisioning
  • Storage Plane Troubleshooting
  • Cluster Health Monitoring

docs.title: Fresh Cluster Cannot Be Activated
docs.text:
Symptom: After a fresh deployment, the cluster cannot be activated. The activation process hangs or fails, and the storage nodes show n/0 disks available in the disks column (sbctl storage-node list).

  1. Remove all storage nodes: sbctl storage-node remove <NODE_ID>. The node must be online or suspended, and the removal shuts the node down itself. --force-remove does not force a removal, but only cancels active tasks of the node.
  2. Delete all storage nodes: sbctl storage-node delete <NODE_ID>
  3. Re-add all storage nodes. The disks should become active.
  4. Try to activate the cluster.

docs.title: Storage Node Health Check Shows Health=False
docs.text:
Symptom: The storage node health check returns health=false (sbctl storage-node list).

  1. First run sbctl storage-node check <NODE_ID>.
  2. If the command keeps showing an unhealthy storage node, shutdown and restart the storage node.

Danger

Never shutdown or restart a storage node while the cluster is in degraded state. This can lead to potential I/O operation. This is independent of the cluster's high-availability status. Check the cluster status with any of the following commands:

sbctl cluster list
sbctl cluster get <cluster-id>
sbctl cluster show <cluster-id>

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text:
Simplyblock regularly provides new releases with new features, performance enhancements, bugfixes, and more.

This section provides detailed information about each simplyblock release, including new features, enhancements, bug fixes, and known issues. Stay informed about the latest developments to ensure optimal performance and take full advantage of simplyblock's capabilities.
Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.2.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Control Plane: The control plane can alternatively deploy into existing Kubernetes clusters and co-locate on workers with storage nodes.
  • Kubernetes Support Matrix: Added OpenShift starting from version 4.19.0
  • OpenStack driver: OpenStack driver is now available. It has support for most optional features and is tested from OpenStack 25.1 (Epoxy). On request, older versions of OS may be supported.
  • The required memory footprint on storage nodes has been reduced from 0.2% of storage capacity to 0.05% of storage capacity.
  • QoS: Pool-level QoS feature has been added.
  • QoS Service Classes: A new feature to assign a service class to a volume. Service classes provide full performance isolation within the cluster.
  • Support for flexible erasure coding schemas within a cluster.
  • Support for RDMA fabric and mixed fabrics (RDMA, TCP)
  • Some write performance improvements during first write to volume and node outage
  • Support for namespace volumes. A single NVMe subsystem can expose up to 32 namespace volumes now

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Control Plane: Fixed a problem, which could lead to stuck deletes.

docs.title: Upgrade Considerations
docs.text: It is possible to upgrade from 25.7.6 and 25.7.7. It is possible to add RDMA support for the fabric during online upgrade.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text: Use of different erasure coding schemas per cluster is available, but can cause I/O interrupt issues in some tests. This feature is experimental and not GA.
Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.3.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text: No new features.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Fixed an issue with FoundationDB where clusters were able to exceed the maximum size of a single entry.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where a default QoS class was assigned to logical volumes.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where a connected wasn't re-established when a node goes down.
  • Storage Plane: Optimized the storage usage calculation of the storage node.

docs.title: Upgrade Considerations
docs.text: It is possible to upgrade from 25.7.6 and 25.7.7. It is possible to add RDMA support for the fabric during the online upgrade.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text: Use of different erasure coding schemas per cluster is available but can cause I/O interrupt issues in some tests. This feature is experimental and not GA.
Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.4.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• The storage node addition tasks (creating partitions and internal devices) are now performed in parallel.
  • The cluster statistics are moved from FoundationDB to Prometheus to increase performance and reduce the memory footprint.
  • The command sbctl now supports the --version (`-v) flag to display the version.
  • The command sbctl storage-node configure now supports the --force flag to format NVMe devices whwn they are already formatted.
  • The command sbctl storage-node add-node now supports the --cores-percentage flag to configure the percentage of cores to be used by the storage node (required on Oracle Linux).
  • The command sbctl storage-node add-node now supports the --nvme-names flag to specify the NVMe device names.
  • The command sbctl storage-node add-node now supports the --format-4k flag to format the NVMe devices with 4K alignment.
  • The command sbctl storage-node add-node now supports the --calculate-hp-only flag to calculate the minimum required huge pages.
  • The commands sbctl cluster create and sbctl cluster add now support the --client-data-nic flag to specify the client data network interface.
  • The command sbctl storage-node now has additional subcommands to list snapshots and volumes by storage node.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Fixed an issue where remote objects weren't correctly removed from the node on receiving distrib events.
  • Control Plane: Improved communication between the control plane and spdk-proxy to avoid race conditions.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of logical volume deletions when multiple delete requests arrive simultaneously.
  • Control Plane: Improved firewall rules management.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where pip packages were installed on cluster update.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue with the calculation of total_mem for multi storage nodes on the same NUMA node.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of device connections when storage nodes connect or disconnect.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the cluster migration tasks.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the cluster health checks.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where core isolation wouldn't correctly work on some systems.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of primary and secondary leader changes.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where additional delete operations would interfere with an asynchronous delete operation already in progress.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where failed devices couldn't be added back to the cluster.
  • Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the storage node status update process.
  • Control Plane: Improved the graceful startup and shutdown of the storage plane.
  • Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where the wrong value was used to configure the hugepages.

docs.title: Upgrade Considerations
docs.text: It is possible to upgrade from 25.10.3.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text: Use of different erasure coding schemas per cluster is available but can cause I/O interrupt issues in some tests. This feature is experimental and not GA.
Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.5.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Storage Plane: Storage nodes and storage clients (via the nvme connect command) can now be force-bound to a specific network interface on their host.
  • Control Plane: The requirement for a route between the control plane nodes and storage plane nodes on the data network interface has been removed.
  • Control Plane: The simplyblock cluster can now be configured with variable port ranges to allow for mitigation of port collisions on specific environments (mostly hyper-converged).
  • Control Plane: The activation speed of large clusters and storage nodes has been improved by parallelizing internal state creation.
  • Control Plane: The restart performance of large clusters has been improved by parallelizing reconnection to other storage nodes.
  • Kubernetes: The CSI driver now automatically reconnects lost NVMe-oF connections on a multipathed logical volume as long as there is at least one healthy connection remaining.
  • Kubernetes: The Kubernetes-based deployment now supports Kubernetes topology management.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Fixed an issue where a new device on a storage node would disappear immediately after being added (new state)..
  • Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues related to journaling and placement which could cause node-affinity issues, I/O interruptions, device formatting issues on 2+2 clusters after multiple 2-node outages in a row.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where multiple outages in a row could cause I/O interruptions.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where deleting a snapshot failed when the logical volumes' primary storage node had an outage.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where DPDK would fail to initialize in rare cases.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where deleting a logical volume failed when the logical volume's secondary storage node was in down state.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the --force option would not work for the device removal.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the get-io-stats command would return the same record for all rows.

docs.title: Upgrade Considerations
docs.text: It is possible to upgrade from 25.10.4 and 25.10.4.2.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• At the moment, unnecessary retries of data migration occur while a storage node is down in m+2 schemas (2+2, 4+2). Data migration should pause once all migratable chunks that haven't been moved yet and resume once all nodes are online. Currently, it retries without success until all nodes are online. Which will be fixed as soon as possible.
  • At the moment, sustaining full fault-tolerance requires more nodes than the theoretical minimum. This is due to a missing feature in the placement, which will be addressed as soon as possible.
  • At the moment it is only possible to define one erasure coding schema per cluster.

docs.title: Features to Expect with Next Major Release
docs.text:
• The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
  • The ability to replicate snapshots to a foreign (remote) simplyblock cluster.
  • The ability to asynchronously replicate volumes via snapshots in regular intervals and support fail-over in Kubernetes.
  • The integration via a new Simplyblock Kubernetes Operator which uses CRDs to specify, create, and track a cluster, storage nodes, volumes, snapshots, and replications.
  • A significant performance optimization during node outages (journal writes).
  • The integration of cluster-internal multipathing for both RDMA- and TCP-based NVMe connections.
  • The ability to send snapshot backups to remote S3-compatible storage.
  • The ability to support multiple NVMe-oF failover connections with one primary and two secondary storage nodes for higher availability.

docs.title: 25.3-PRE
docs.text:
Simplyblock is happy to release the pre-release version of the upcoming Simplyblock 25.3.

Warning

This is a pre-release and may contain issues. It is not recommended for production use.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
Simplyblock strives to provide a strong product. Following is a list of the enhancements and features that made it into this release.

  • High availability has been significantly hardened for production. Main improvements concern the support for safe and interruption free fail-over and fail-back in different types of outage scenarios. Those include: partial network outage, full network outage, host failure, container failure, reboots, graceful and ungraceful shutdowns of nodes. Tested for single und dial node outages.
  • Multiple journal compression bugs have been identified and fixed.
  • Multiple journal fail-over bugs have been identified and fixed.
  • Logical volume creation, deletion, snapshotting, and resizing can now be performed via a secondary storage node (when the primary storage node is offline).
  • The system has been hardened against high load scenarios, determined by the amount of parallel NVMe-oF volumes per node, the amount of storage and parallel I/O. Tested up to 400 concurrent and fully active logical volumes per node and u to 20 concurrent I/O processes per logical volume.
  • Erasure coding schemes 2+1, 2+2, 4+2, 4+4 have been made power-fail-safe with high-availability enabled.
  • System has been extensively tested outside of AWS with KVM-based virtualization and on bare-metal deployments.
  • Significant rework of the command line tool sbcli to simplify commands and parameters and make it more consistent. For more information see Important Changes.
  • Support for Linux Core Isolation to improve performance and system stability.
  • Added support for Proxmox via the simplyblock Proxmox integration.

docs.title: Important Changes
docs.text:
Simplyblock made significant changes to the command line tool sbcli to simplify working with it. Many parameters and commands were meant for internal testing and confusing to users. Hence, simplyblock decided to make those private.

Parameters and commands that were made private should not influence users. If the change to private for a parameter or command affects a deployment, reach out to simplyblock support.

Most changes are backward-compatible, however, some are not. Following is a list of all changes.

  • Command: storage-node
    • Renamed command sn to storage-node (sn still works as an alias)
    • Changed subcommand device-testing-mode to private
    • Changed subcommand info-spdk to private
    • Changed subcommand remove-jm-device to private
    • Changed subcommand send-cluster-map to private
    • Changed subcommand get-cluster-map to private
    • Changed subcommand dump-lvstore to private

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
Simplyblock always seeks to provide a stable and strong release. However, smaller known issues happen. Following is a list of known issues of the current simplyblock release.

Info

This is a pre-release and many of those known issues are expected to be resolved with the final release.

  • The control plane reaches a limit at around 2,200 logical volumes.
  • If a storage node goes offline while a logical volume is being deleted, the storage cluster may keep some garbage.
  • In rare cases, resizing a logical volume under high I/O load may cause a storage node restart.
  • If a storage cluster reaches its capacity limit and runs full, file systems on logical volumes may return I/O errors.
  • A fail-back after a fail-over may increase to >10s (with freezing I/O) with a larger number of logical volumes per storage node (>100 logical volumes).
  • A fail-over time may increase to >5s (with freezing I/O) on large logical volumes (>5 TB).
  • During a node outage, I/O performance may drop significantly with certain I/O patterns due to a performance issue in the journal compression.
  • Journal compression may cause significant I/O performance drops (10-20s) in periodic intervals under certain I/O load patterns, especially when the logical volume capacity reaches its limits for the first time.
  • A peak read IOPS performance regression has been observed.
  • In rare cases, a primary-secondary storage node combination may get into a flip-flop situation with multiple fail-over/fail-back iterations due to network or configuration issues of particular logical volumes or clients.
  • A secondary node may get stuck when trying to restart under high load (>100 logical volumes).
  • Node affinity rules are not considered after a storage node migration to a new host.
  • Return code of sbcli commands is always 0.
Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.6.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
Simplyblock strives to provide a strong product. Following is a list of the enhancements and features that made it into this release.

  • General: Renamed sbcli to sbctl. The old sbcli command is deprecated but still available as a fallback for scripts.
  • Storage Plane: Increased maximum of available logical volumes per storage node to 1,000.
  • Storage Plane: Added the option to start multiple storage nodes in parallel on the same host. This is useful for machines with multiple NUMA nodes and many CPU cores to increase scalability.
  • Storage Plane: Added NVMe multipathing independent high-availability between storage nodes to harden resilience against network issues and improve failover.
  • Storage Plane: Removed separate secondary storage nodes for failover. From now on, all storage nodes act as primary and secondary storage nodes.
  • Storage Plane: Added I/O redirection in case of failover to secondary to improve cluster stability and failover times.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for CPU Core Isolation to improve performance consistency. Core masks and core isolation are auto-applied on disaggregated setups.
  • Storage Plane: Added sbctl storage-node configure command to automate the configuration of new storage nodes. See the CLI reference for more information.
  • Storage Plane: Added optimized algorithms for the 4+1 and 4+2 erasure coding configurations.
  • Storage Plane: Reimplemented the Quality of Service (QoS) subsystem with significant less overhead than the old one.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for namespaced logical volumes (experimental).
  • Storage Plane: Reimplemented the initialization of a new page to significantly improve the performance of first write to page issues.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for optional labels when using strict anti-affinity.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for node affinity in case of a device failure to try to recover onto another device on the host.
  • Proxmox: Added support for native Proxmox node migration.
  • Talos: Added support to deploy on Talos-based OS-images.
  • AWS: Added Bottlerocket support.
  • AWS: Added multipathing support for Amazon Linux 2, Amazon Linux 2023, Bottlerocket.
  • GCP: Added support for Google Compute Engine.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Storage Plane: Fixed a critical issue on cluster expansion during rebalancing.
  • Storage Plane: Optimized internal journal compression of meta-data to use fewer CPU resources.
  • Storage Plane: Significantly improved the fail-back time in failover situations.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed a CRC checksum error that occurred in rare situations after a node outage.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed a conflict resolution issue with could lead to data corruption in failover scenarios.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed a segmentation fault after resizing multiple logical volumes in a fast sequence.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed data placement issues which could lead to unexpected I/O interruptions after a sequence of outages.
  • Storage Plane: Reduced huge pages consumption by about 1.5x. Huge pages are automatically recalculated on node restart.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed an RPC issue on clusters with eight or more storage nodes.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed a race condition on storage node restarts or cluster reactivations.
  • Storage Plane: Hardened a health-check issue which affected multiple services.
  • Storage Plane: Improved shared buffers calculation on large storage nodes.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed an issue in the metadata journal which could lead to a temporary conflict and I/O interruption on the fail-back of large logical volumes.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where a storage node would stay unhealthy after a cluster upgrade.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where the internal journal devices would fail to automatically reconnect after a cluster outage.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where a restart of one storage node could lead to a crash on another storage node.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed reattaching Amazon EBS volumes when migrating a storage node to a new host.
  • Control Plane: Improved error handling on the internal controller code base.
  • Control Plane: Fixed a range of false-positive detections that lead to unexpected storage node restarts or, in rare cases, cluster suspension.
  • Control Plane: Cleaned up the API from unnecessary calls and fixed smaller response content issues.
  • Control Plane: Improved handling of Graylog in case of primary management node failover.
  • Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues regarding spill-over and outages in case of a management node disk running full.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the generated logical volume connection string is missing the logical volume id in the NQN.
  • Control Plane: Fixed multiple build issues with ARM64 CPUs.
  • Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues when deleting logical volumes and snapshots which could lead to dangling garbage and inconsistencies.
  • Control Plane: Fixed a primary storage node restart bug.
  • Control Plane: Improved NVMe device detection by switching from serial number to PCIe address.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue, related to logical volume operations, where FoundationDB's memory consumption would continue to increase over time.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where migration tasks would stale with status mig error: 8, retrying.
  • Control Plane: Improved observability by polling thread information from SPDK and store it in Prometheus.
  • Control Plane: Improved the performance of parallel logical volume creations.
  • Control Plane: Fixed data unit of read_speed in the Grafana cluster dashboard.
  • Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the PromAgent image wouldn't be upgraded on a cluster upgrade.
  • Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where the CSI driver would hang if it tries to delete a snapshot in error state.
  • Kubernetes: Fixed hanging NVMe/TCP connections in the CSI driver on storage node restarts or failovers.
  • Kubernetes: Fixed an issue with failing volume snapshots.
  • Kubernetes: Improved the version pinning of required services.
  • Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where NVMe/TCP connections in multipathing setups would be disconnected in the wrong order.
  • Proxmox: Improved automatic reconnecting of volumes after storage node restarts and failovers.

docs.title: Important Changes
docs.text:
• Architecture: Separate secondary nodes have been removed as a concept. Instead, in a high-availability cluster, every deployed primary storage node also acts as a secondary storage node to another primary.
  • Storage Plane: NVMe devices are now identified by their serial number to enable PCIe renumbering in case of changes to the system configuration.
  • Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port range TCP/8080-8890 was changed to TCP/8080-8180. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
  • Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port range TCP/9090-9900 was changed to TCP/9100-9200. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
  • Firewall rules adjustment: A new port range TCP/9030-9059 was added. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
  • Firewall rules adjustment: A new port range TCP/9060-9099 was added. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
  • Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port TCP/4420 has been removed. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
  • Image registry: The image registry moved from Amazon ECR to DockerHub.

docs.text: Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 26.2-PRE.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Storage Plane: Added support for DH-CHAP and transport layer security (TLS) for the storage plane and communication between NVMe targets and initiators.
  • Storage Plane: Added support volume backup and restore. The new mechanism takes backups of snapshots and sends the snapshot-chains to an S3-compatible storage. Backup retention, merge policies, and auto-backup schedules are configured via the operator. Snapshots can be restored into volumes (PVCs) on the same cluster or into a different cluster. Backup is storage-efficient (delta-only, compressed).
  • Storage Plane: Added support for remote snapshot replication. Snapshots can be asynchronously replicated btw. nodes and sites in a network-efficient manner.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for asynchronous replication which adds the ability to automatically failing-over and failing-back of selected volumes across sites with a certain time-gap/backlog (e.g., 5 minutes). This is useful for slow links and provides significantly better RTO (zero) and RPO (minimum: 1 minute) than traditional backups.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for FTT 2 (failure to tolerate) which enables up to two failover paths. When enabled, simplyblock creates three communication paths between the initiators and the NVMe targets (primary, secondary, and tertiary) with identical subsystems able to process I/O. This allows the loss or maintenance of any two nodes in the cluster, regardless of the combination, at a point in time.
  • Storage Plane: Added support for full multipathing within the storage cluster and between initiators and NVMe targets. This means that clients can have four (FTT=1) or six (FTT=2) connections via separate VLANs using separate networking paths. Each endpoint-combination uses two separate connections through the available network paths. It has advantages over simple bonding and multi-chassis link aggregation groups (MLAG).
  • Kubernetes: Added support for OpenShift-managed TLS certificates for communication within the control plane and cluster endpoints.
  • Kubernetes: Added support for mutual TLS (mTLS) on the control plane, using cert-manager-issued certificates.
  • Kubernetes: Added support for offloading volume encryption keys to an external KMS (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao).
  • Kubernetes: Added support for namespaced volumes, which auto-create subsystems and namespaces within those subsystems in a pre-defined ratio (e.g., 8 or 16 namespaces per subsystem) in Kubernetes-based environments. The ratio can be configured via the operator.
  • Kubernetes: Added a new, experimental Kubernetes operator to simplify the deployment of simplyblock control planes, storage planes, and the CSI driver in Kubernetes-based environments, such as OpenShift and Talos.
  • General: All container images are now based on RHEL 10 base images and use Python 3.12. This solves multiple open CVEs and additional vulnerabilities.

  • The parameters --crypto-key1 and --crypto-key2 have been deprecated and cannot be used anymore. Encryption keys are now handled through the KMS-based system.

docs.title: Features to Expect with Next Major Release
docs.text:
• The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
  • A significant performance optimization during node outages (journal writes).
  • The ability to live migrate volumes between storage clusters.
  • Inline data integrity validation to prevent silent data corruption.
  • Support for failure domains, spreading data, journal copies, and failover paths across racks, cabinets, or availability zones.

Simplyblock is happy to release Simplyblock 26.3. The changes are grouped by the component they belong to: the simplyblock control plane and storage plane, and the Kubernetes components, meaning the Simplyblock Operator and Simplyblock CSI.

docs.title: Simplyblock
docs.text: The control plane and the storage plane are released together and share a version number. The changes below apply to every deployment, including a Kubernetes-based one.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Added asynchronous replication between two storage clusters. Several destinations per cluster are supported, the cadence and the retention are set per replication policy, and a failover is requested for a single volume, a whole policy, or a whole destination.
  • Control Plane: Added the planned cross-cluster cutover, by which a volume is handed over to another cluster under control. The remaining delta is shrunk, the source is fenced, and the client is moved to the target. The return to a recovered source runs as a delta, and the return to a fresh cluster as a full copy.
  • Control Plane: Added support for failure domains. Data chunks, parity chunks, journal copies, and the secondary and tertiary nodes are spread across distinct domains, with a host-disjoint fallback and a warning where that is not possible.
  • Control Plane: Added online storage node removal, which runs as a resumable background task and re-hosts the replicas and devices the node holds, and the expansion of an FTT 2 cluster by a single node. Several nodes are now added in parallel.
  • Control Plane: Added cluster-wide maintenance operations. Every node of a cluster is restarted in one step, and the creation, deletion, and modification of volumes, snapshots, clones, and pools is refused and resumed for the whole cluster. Read paths and the restarts, migrations, and repairs a cluster performs on itself are unaffected.
  • Control Plane: Added release-specific upgrade plug-ins, which run their preparation step before a cluster update and their completion step after it, and record the installed release on the cluster.
  • Control Plane: Added batch migration of namespaced volumes, by which every volume that shares an NVMe-oF subsystem is moved as one coordinated group. What a failed migration left behind on the target is removed idempotently.
  • Control Plane: Added quorum-based device exclusion. A device that draws I/O errors from a quorum of the other online nodes is excluded cluster-wide, independent of what its NVMe controller reports, which is the case a slow-but-connected device previously slipped through. A device whose latency deviates from the cluster average is reported as a warning event before it fails.
  • Control Plane: Added alerting from the cluster event log, which provisions Grafana rules that read the transition an entity made rather than the state it ended in. Journal events are now collected into the event log next to the distrib events.
  • Control Plane: Added a FoundationDB exporter with its own dashboard, request metrics of the management API, the device health information the storage plane holds, and a retention period of 30 days for cluster tasks and their logs.
  • Control Plane: Added a rebalance operation to the cluster API, validation of the erasure coding scheme by the management API, and independent NVMe device filters for a storage node, where the device model and the size range are accepted alone as well as together.
  • Storage Plane: The journal device of a node is now a RAID 0+1 stack instead of an N-way mirror across the journal partition of every drive. Write amplification is capped at two physical writes per journal record and per node, independent of the drive count, and a drive lifecycle event rebuilds the affected leg instead of the whole mirror.
  • Storage Plane: Added a second generation of distrib write protection. A new cluster is created on it, and an upgraded cluster is moved over once every online node has migrated. An offline node is brought over by its next restart.
  • Storage Plane: The ANA state change of a volume is now scoped to its namespace instead of the whole subsystem. A volume that shares its subsystem with other volumes is failed over, suspended, and migrated without moving their I/O to the other node.
  • Storage Plane: The core allocation of a storage node gives the distrib and poller threads their share before alceml, which takes its device-scaled count from what is left. Explicit layouts are added for hosts with two to five vCPUs.
  • General: Added diagnostics for a latency or crash investigation: the bdev latency histograms with a per-layer probe, by which a tail-latency spike is localized to a layer of the bdev stack, and the host directory /var/crash mounted into the storage plane container, so that a core dump survives the container.
  • General: Updated the packages inherited from the container base images and dropped wget from the image, to resolve open CVEs.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Fixed the loss of I/O during a storage node restart, where an unbounded operation inside the port fence could outlast the client keep-alive.
  • Control Plane: Improved the recovery of a cluster after a full reboot. An activation that wedged is detected by a watchdog, automatic reactivation is gated on every node being online, and a suspended cluster is drained to all-offline before it is restarted.
  • Control Plane: Fixed storage nodes flapping to the down state on a health probe timeout, and a node that is down no longer counts toward the suspension of the cluster. The suspension is gated on an actual loss of the data plane rather than on an unreachable management network.
  • Control Plane: Fixed three ways in which a highly available volume could silently lose one of its paths, and the duplicate paths a repair left behind are now pruned. No leadership over an lvstore is granted while a restart or a recovery task owns the movement of it.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the failover of a namespaced volume, which the kernel rejected with mismatching identifiers.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the deletion pipeline of volumes and snapshots. A delete the cluster cannot complete is refused rather than accepted, a deferred delete completes once the node it waited for returns, and concurrent operations on one snapshot chain are mutually exclusive, which closes a corruption of the blob tree.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the migration of a volume whose snapshot chain spans several nodes, of an encrypted volume, and of a volume with a tertiary node. A migration whose source node goes offline is suspended instead of being cleaned up on the target.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the replication of the blob chain of a volume, which replicated only the snapshots of the volume itself. A failover only ever targets a fully replicated and live snapshot, and a replication no longer halts silently under back-pressure.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the addition of a storage node, which aborted on a lock timeout, on a stale in-creation record, or on an already provisioned device slot, and which did not survive the CPU topology reboot. A re-entry is idempotent now, and the status of a node, a device, a cluster, and a volume is written through a compare-and-set operation, so that a crashed writer cannot leave a stale status behind.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the capacity reporting, which mixed raw with effective capacity, and the cluster admission check, which did not count the utilization of snapshots. On a storage pool, the capacity check of a resize no longer counts the volume being resized twice.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the cloning of an encrypted volume, for which the crypto layer was missing from the recorded bdev stack, the key management of the local KMS, and the rendering of secrets in the management API.
  • Control Plane: Fixed a forced storage node shutdown that could block indefinitely, a cluster that grew by being reactivated, a cluster expansion that did not reattach the sibling failover of its donor node, and the leases of long-running tasks, which expired while the task was still running.
  • Control Plane: Improved the throughput of the snapshot and volume monitors, which process chains and nodes in parallel, and the logging to Graylog, which is written non-blocking, so that a slow log target no longer holds up the control plane.
  • Storage Plane: Improved the reliability of the graceful startup and the graceful shutdown of the storage plane. A storage plane whose RPC endpoint hangs on a live process is aborted instead of being waited for, and the wait for the journal replication of a peer is bounded, so that it cannot defer a restart indefinitely.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed the roles of the hub volumes, which are active on both sides within a node and passive between nodes, and the hub volume subsystem, which was lost across a restart.
  • Storage Plane: Fixed the re-admission of the devices of a node recovering from an outage, which was silently refused while the node had not yet reached the online state. The memory footprint of a node improved as well, since the small I/O buffers are sized from the subsystem count of the cluster.

docs.title: New Features in 26.3.1
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Added the alerts endpoint, GET /api/v2/clusters/<CLUSTER_UUID>/alerts/, which returns the conditions that currently need an operator.
  • Control Plane: Added hard per-object limits, enforced on every create and resize: 70 TiB per volume, 100 snapshots per volume, and 500 clones per snapshot. See Limits.
  • Control Plane: The shared NVMe-oF subsystems of a storage node are aligned with the storage pools, so that a subsystem carries the namespaces of exactly one pool.
  • Control Plane: Added the self-repair of a device left unavailable or removed, unless it was removed by the operator.
  • Control Plane: Added the Grafana rule API_request_latency_high, which fires when the mean request latency of the control plane API stays above 15 seconds.

docs.title: Fixes in 26.3.1
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Fixed the client I/O errors during the restart of a primary storage node, where a non-leader peer kept accepting I/O through a half-demoted lvstore.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the loss of the last usable path on a graceful shutdown, where the hublvol controller of a secondary or tertiary node was detached along with it.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the Invalid Namespace or Format error a client received from a subsystem that became reachable before its namespaces were attached.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the silent partial registration of the volume subsystems during an lvstore rebuild.
  • Control Plane: Fixed a volume deletion that stalled after its data had been freed, because the lvstore leadership moved while the asynchronous delete was running.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the journal geometry across an upgrade, where an existing journal could be rebuilt under the newer RAID layout.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the silent acceptance of a storage plane that was started without the NVMe options of the control plane.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the admission of a snapshot, which did not charge the utilized size of its source volume against the storage pool and the cluster.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the upgrade of a storage node whose record still carries the legacy lvstore_stack_secondary and lvstore_stack_tertiary values.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the flooding of the cluster event log with journal compression events, of which only a failure is persisted now.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the filesystem metrics of the node exporter, which were read from the wrong root path.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the handling of a FoundationDB backup, whose retention metadata was not recorded.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the log collection bundle, which aborted in Docker mode on a missing kubeconfig.
  • Control Plane: Fixed a fatal Python error at the shutdown of the storage node proxy, whose statistics thread outlived the interpreter.
  • Control Plane: Fixed the log levels of the management API and of the Docker Swarm services.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text: The changes below apply to Kubernetes-based deployments only. They are delivered by the Simplyblock Operator and by Simplyblock CSI.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Operator: Added support for failure domains, by which erasure coding chunks and failover paths are spread across racks or availability zones. Workers are assigned to a domain through the StorageNodeSet, and the effective domain of a worker is reflected in the status of the StorageNode.
  • Operator: Added support for several StorageNodeSet resources per storage cluster, by which workers with different hardware or a different role are enrolled with their own configuration, and for the parallel addition of storage nodes.
  • Operator: Added live volume migration through the new VolumeMigration resource, by which the backing logical volume is moved between storage nodes while the volume stays online. The new NVMe-oF paths on the target node are validated on every consuming worker before the migration is continued.
  • Operator: Added the storage node drain, removal, and host migration workflows, requested with a StorageNodeOps resource. A removal suspends the node, migrates its volumes to the remaining nodes, verifies the result, and removes the node, and a migration relocates the identity of a storage node to a different worker.
  • Operator: Added support for asynchronous replication between two storage clusters, declared with the new ReplicationPair, ReplicationPolicy, and ReplicationSlot resources. Failover and failback are requested with a ReplicationOps resource, scoped to a replication target, a policy, or a single volume, and a PVC is enrolled into a policy through an annotation.
  • Operator: Added automatic, latency-based volume rebalancing and back storage data realignment, which are configured per cluster and triggered independently of each other.
  • Operator: Added support for topology-aware provisioning across several storage clusters, by which a volume is provisioned in the cluster that matches the topology of the consuming workload, the option to skip the creation of the FoundationDB cluster, and the adoption of an existing Helm-deployed storage cluster, storage pool, and storage nodes into the operator resources.
  • Operator: Added configuration of the image pull policy, the resource limits, and the SPDK system memory of the storage node workloads, and of a custom OpenShift MachineConfigPool, so that storage nodes are rebooted through a pool that is separate from the remaining workers. Every image reference is validated against the trusted registries, and a field that cannot be changed after creation is rejected instead of being ignored silently.
  • Operator: The Thanos data of the monitoring stack is now stored in MinIO instead of a filesystem-backed object store, and Prometheus can be deployed with more than one replica.
  • CSI Driver: Added support for co-locating the primary storage node of a volume with the worker that runs the consuming pod, and for the migration of namespaced volumes together with the coordinated restart of all pods that share an NVMe subsystem.
  • CSI Driver: Added the detection and the repair of stale NVMe-oF subsystems and controllers on a worker.
  • CSI Driver: The presence of a device is registered when the volume is connected, instead of only by polling, and the host NQN and the DH-CHAP secrets are forwarded at that point.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Operator: Fixed the release of the NVMe target paths of a migration that never reaches its cutover, and the rebuild of the storage node configuration after an operator restart with an in-flight storage node migration.
  • Operator: Fixed the StoragePool resource remaining in Terminating when its backend UUID was never set, and the PVC validator, which did not accept all of the volume placement annotations.
  • CSI Driver: Fixed incompatibilities when formatting and mounting ext4 and XFS volumes, and the connection of a volume in a cluster with more than one storage pool.
  • CSI Driver: Fixed the loss of the kernel module configuration on the host, which was written into the ephemeral filesystem of the storage node container and was gone after the CPU topology reboot during a node addition.
  • CSI Driver: Fixed the restart loop of the CSI controller container, caused by dangling snapshots and volumes of a removed cluster. A gRPC keepalive and a connection timeout now detect a broken connection to a control plane instead of blocking a request.
  • Operator and CSI Driver: Updated the container base images and the Go dependencies to resolve open CVEs.

docs.title: Fixes in 26.3.1
docs.text:
• Operator: Fixed the deletion of a StoragePool with DHCHAP enabled, which stayed in Terminating because the update dropping its finalizer was rejected by its own validation.
  • Operator: Fixed the creation of a StoragePool with DHCHAP enabled and an empty allowedNodes, which is rejected now, since such a pool can never provision a volume.
  • Operator: Fixed the generated StorageClass of a DHCHAP pool, whose allowedTopologies term matched no node.
  • Operator: Fixed the label marking the allowed nodes of a StoragePool, which is keyed by the pool UUID now and can no longer exceed the 63 bytes a label name allows.
  • Operator: Fixed the failback of a replicated volume, whose target cluster, pool, and volume were not resolved through the relationship lookup.
  • Operator: Fixed the list of owned custom resource definitions in the cluster service version.
  • Operator: Updated golang.org/x/crypto and the etcd client to resolve three high severity advisories.
  • CSI Driver: Fixed the connection monitor, whose repair pass tore down a path that its reconcile pass had created moments earlier.

docs.title: Important Changes
docs.text:
• The storage plane sizing of a node moves to the cluster. The flags --max-subsys, --hugepages-mem, and --vcpu-count are set on sbctl cluster create and sbctl cluster add, and a node adopts them when it is added and on every restart. --max-subsys, --max-size, and --cores-percentage are removed from sbctl storage-node configure, and --max-subsys and --max-size from sbctl storage-node restart. The flag --max-lvol is renamed to --max-subsys, which is what it has always limited.
  • The core budget of the storage plane is an absolute vCPU count instead of a percentage. A node that cannot satisfy the count of its cluster, plus one core for the system, is refused instead of running on fewer cores than requested. sbctl cluster update --vcpu-count does not exist, because rewriting the core mask of every node belongs to a deliberate redeployment.
  • A configured subsystem limit above 75 per storage node is rejected, where it was accepted and then clamped silently before, so a node reserved huge pages for subsystems it could never serve. An lvstore serves at most 6000 objects, counting volumes, clones, and snapshots, and a create beyond that limit is refused.
  • Failure domains are a deploy-time feature. A cluster cannot be upgraded into them, and --enable-failure-domain has to be set at creation time. Once it is set, --failure-domain is mandatory on every sbctl storage-node add-node and rejected on a cluster without the feature.
  • sbctl storage-node remove no longer migrates the data of the node. The node has to host no volumes and no snapshots, and those are migrated beforehand. The flag --force-remove no longer removes volumes and snapshots, it cancels the active tasks of the node before the removal starts.
  • The commands sbctl storage-node resume, sbctl storage-node get-bdevs, and sbctl storage-node unload are removed. Instead of resume, sbctl storage-node restart has to be used.
  • The command sbctl cluster add-replication is deprecated. Instead, the commands sbctl cluster replication-target-add and sbctl cluster replication-policy-add have to be used, which support more than one destination per cluster.
  • sbctl volume migrate only pre-creates the target subsystem and returns the migration id and the NVMe connect strings. The flags --deadline and --max-retries move to sbctl volume migrate-continue, which advances the migration once the client is connected.
  • After sbctl cluster update, two commands have to be run. sbctl cluster upgrade-complete releases the journal compression hold the update took across its rolling restart and records the installed release, and sbctl cluster switch-write-protection moves the cluster to the second generation of distrib write protection, on which it does not land by itself.
  • The flag --all is removed from sbctl snapshot list, which gained --lvol-id, --node-id, and --json. The flag --cluster-id is removed from sbctl backup restore, whose cluster is derived from the backup.
  • The Pool resource is renamed to StoragePool, and the resource enrolling a group of workers is renamed from StorageNode to StorageNodeSet. The name StorageNode is now used for the per-worker resource that is created by the operator.
  • The field maxLogicalVolumeCount is renamed to maxSubsystemCount, and the field corePercentage is removed. Storage node sizing is moved from the StorageNodeSet to the cluster scope, and the field partitions is replaced by enableJournalDevice.
  • The deprecated StorageCluster fields blockSize, qpairCount, pageSizeInBlocks, maxQueueSize, inflightIOThreshold, strictNodeAntiAffinity, haType, isSingleNode, and clientQpairCount are removed.
  • The StorageCluster spec field maxFaultTolerance is replaced by maxConcurrentWorkerRestarts, which is capped at the fault tolerance of the cluster. The backend-reported maxFaultTolerance remains part of the status.
  • The field unpinBeforeDrain is removed. A pinned volume has to be unpinned manually before its storage node is drained.
  • The volume placement annotations are unified into simplyblock.io/selected-storage-node. On a new PVC, a host id supplied through simplyblock.io/host-id or simplybk/host-id is rewritten into that annotation and treated as a pin. On a pre-existing PVC, both legacy annotations are still honored as the lowest-priority source of the primary storage node.

docs.title: Upgrade Considerations
docs.text:
• The CSI driver added an extended check to prevent an accidental filesystem format onto an existing pre-formatted volume in one of the upstream CSI libraries. To ensure all existing volumes work as expected, users are highly encouraged to run this script after upgrading to 26.3.0. Annotate existing PVCs Script ⧉
  • An upgrade from the previous R25 Helm chart to the R26 Operator installation requires a maintenance window and additional steps. See the Upgrade Procedure R25 to R26 for details.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• At the moment it is only possible to define one erasure coding schema per cluster.

  • When deleting pods with simplyblock-backed PVCs, it is important to delete the pod first, before deleting the PVC.

    Deleting a pod before its persistent volume claim
    kubectl delete pod <pod-name> --wait=true
kubectl delete pvc <pvc-name> --wait=true

  • A full FTT 1 or FTT 2 network outage can create a situation where surviving nodes lose access to the last journal records. This can cause loss of I/O availability until at least one node is restarted.

  • Node Removal currently only works with online nodes.

docs.title: Features to Expect with Next Major Release
docs.text:
• The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
  • Inline data integrity validation to prevent silent data corruption.

Simplyblock is happy to release Simplyblock 26.4. The changes are grouped by the component they belong to: the simplyblock control plane and storage plane, and the Kubernetes components, meaning the Simplyblock Operator and Simplyblock CSI.

Draft

This page is a work in progress. Only the important changes of the operator API are collected so far. The control plane and storage plane entries, the operator and CSI driver features, the upgrade path, and the known issues are not final yet.

docs.title: Simplyblock
docs.text: The control plane and the storage plane are released together and share a version number. The changes below apply to every deployment, including a Kubernetes-based one.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Control Plane: Added secondary indices to the control plane's FoundationDB store. A lookup by anything other than the record id, such as the volumes of a storage pool or the node a device sits in, is answered from an index instead of a scan of the whole record class, so the cost of a lookup no longer grows with the size of the cluster. The indices of an upgraded cluster are backfilled by sbctl cluster upgrade-complete, and until an index is complete its reads fall back to a scan.
  • Control Plane: Added sbctl cluster build-indices, sbctl cluster check-indices, and sbctl cluster index-state to operate those indices. The backfill is idempotent and safe to run against a live cluster, check-indices writes back what it can derive with --repair, and index-state lists where every index stands and takes a single one out of service with --set disabled.
  • Control Plane: TODO, to be collected from the sbcli changes since 26.3.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Control Plane: TODO, to be collected from the sbcli changes since 26.3.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text: The changes below apply to a Kubernetes-based deployment and ship with the Simplyblock Operator and Simplyblock CSI.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text: • Operator: TODO, to be collected from the simplyblock-operator changes since 26.3.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Operator: TODO, to be collected from the simplyblock-operator changes since 26.3.

docs.title: Important Changes
docs.text:
The operator API moves from storage.simplyblock.io/v1alpha1 to storage.simplyblock.io/v1alpha2. Every kind is served at the new version, which is also the storage version, and a conversion webhook translates an existing v1alpha1 object so that a manifest written for 26.3 keeps working. The replication kinds are the exception and stay at v1alpha1.

  • Imperative operations are separate resources instead of fields on the entity they act on. Setting StorageCluster.spec.action is replaced by creating a StorageClusterOps, and the operation runs to a terminal phase and stays afterward as the record of what was done. StorageClusterOps, StorageNodeOps, StorageDeviceOps, StoragePoolOps, PersistentVolumeOps, StorageBackupOps, ControlPlaneOps, and OperatorOps share that shape, including spec.abort and the Aborted phase.
  • A storage cluster is deployed from a ClusterDeploymentConfig. The operator inspects the workers, writes the draft, and an administrator approves it with spec.approved, after which the document is expanded into the StorageCluster and its StorageNode objects. The document is immutable once approved.
  • A namespace holds at most one StorageCluster. A second storage cluster needs a namespace of its own.
  • Every enum value of the group is PascalCase. An action such as restart is written Restart, and a phase such as Completed is written Succeeded.
  • The status of a running operation is a state machine snapshot in status.step, replacing status.subPhase. status.step.state carries the step, and status.step.deadline is when that step expires.
  • The annotation and label keys move from the simplyblock.io/ prefix to storage.simplyblock.io/. Every spelling is read and the new one is written, so nothing has to be relabeled. The exception is simplyblock.io/pod-affinity, which has no prefixed spelling yet.
  • The StorageCluster finalizer is renamed from storage.simplyblock.io/cluster-finalizer to storage.simplyblock.io/storagecluster-finalizer. The old key is read for one release.

docs.title: Renamed and Retired Resources
docs.text:
A kind that is absorbed is not converted. The upgrade constructs the successor, and a manifest that creates the old kind has to be rewritten.

26.3 resource 26.4 resource Notes VolumeMigration PersistentVolumeOps Cluster-scoped, because a PersistentVolume is. Action Migrate. BackupRestore StorageBackupOps Absorbed as spec.action: Restore, the kind's only action. BackupPolicy StorageBackupPolicy Selects its claims by label instead of a per-claim annotation. BackupImport Retired The backup store is the inventory, so a backup another cluster wrote needs no import. StorageNodeSet StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes The fleet template. The workers move to ClusterDeploymentConfig. Task StorageCluster.status.tasks Canceled with a StorageClusterOps carrying action: CancelTask.

docs.title: StorageCluster
docs.text:
26.3 property 26.4 property Notes spec.maxHugePagesSize spec.minHugePagesSize The value is a minimum and always was. spec.hashicorpVaultSettings.baseURL spec.kms.vault.endpoint spec.backup.localEndpoint spec.backup.endpoint bucket, prefix, and region are added. spec.openShiftCluster spec.storageNodes.openshift spec.storageNodes.openShiftMachineConfigPool spec.storageNodes.openshift.machineConfigPool spec.enableDataRealignment spec.disableDataRealignment Inverted. Realignment is on by default now. spec.volumeAutoPlacement.enabled spec.enableVolumeAutoPlacement Moves up to the cluster spec. spec.volumeAutoPlacement.migrationEnabled spec.volumeAutoPlacement.disableMigration Inverted. spec.volumeAutoPlacement.latencyBenchmarkEnabled spec.volumeAutoPlacement.enableLatencyBenchmark spec.volumeMigrationSettings.enabled Removed Migration cannot be turned off. spec.action StorageClusterOps status.actionStatus StorageClusterOps.status

An inverted field is the dangerous row of this release. A spec that still carries enableDataRealignment or migrationEnabled is accepted by the API server and ignored, and the feature runs with the opposite default.

docs.title: StorageClusterOps
docs.text:
26.3 property 26.4 property spec.nodeRollingRestart spec.rollingRestart status.nodeRollingRestartStatus status.rollingRestart status.triggered Removed

The action node-recycle is renamed to RollingRestart, and activate, expand, shutdown, start, and restart become Activate, Expand, Shutdown, Start, and Restart. CancelTask is added.

docs.title: StorageNode
docs.text: 26.3 property 26.4 property Notes spec.storageNodeSetRef spec.clusterRef and spec.nodeSet The node is owned by its cluster. spec.socketIndex spec.slot spec.overrides spec.config config.failureDomain config.failureDomain Was an integer index, is a label value such as rack-a. spec.skipKubeletConfiguration StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes.enableKubeletConfiguration Inverted, and per cluster. overrides.enableCpuTopology StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes.enableCpuTopology Per cluster, not per node.

docs.title: StorageNodeOps
docs.text:
26.3 property 26.4 property Notes spec.storageNodeRef spec.nodeRef spec.targetWorkerNode spec.migrate.targetWorkerNode spec.newSsdPcie spec.migrate.newSsdPcie spec.drain spec.remove Matches the action it parameterizes. status.subPhase status.step.state status.volumesMigrated status.drain.volumesMigrated status.volumesPending status.drain.volumesTotal A total instead of a remainder. status.triggered Removed

The six actions become Shutdown, Restart, Suspend, Resume, Remove, and Migrate, and HostMaintenance is added. The sub-phases Migrating and Restarting of a migration become the steps Relocating and AwaitingNode, and the Migrating sub-phase of a removal becomes MigratingVolumes.

docs.title: StoragePool
docs.text:
26.3 property 26.4 property spec.clusterName spec.clusterRef spec.capacityLimit spec.limits.capacity spec.logicalVolumeMaxSize spec.limits.maxVolumeSize spec.qos.iops spec.limits.iops spec.qos.throughput spec.limits.throughput spec.dhchap spec.volumeDefaults.enableDHCHAP spec.storageClassParameters.qosRwIops spec.volumeDefaults.iops spec.storageClassParameters.qosRwMbytes spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.readWrite spec.storageClassParameters.qosRMbytes spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.read spec.storageClassParameters.qosWMbytes spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.write spec.storageClassParameters.encryption spec.volumeDefaults.enableEncryption spec.storageClassParameters.maxNamespacePerSubsys spec.volumeDefaults.maxNamespacesPerSubsystem spec.storageClassParameters.fabric spec.volumeDefaults.fabric spec.storageClassParameters.filesystem spec.volumeDefaults.filesystem spec.storageClassParameters.tune2fsReservedBlocks spec.volumeDefaults.tune2fsReservedBlocks spec.action, spec.status Removed

spec.limits is mutable, so a capacity or a QoS ceiling is raised on a running pool. spec.volumeDefaults is immutable, because the parameters of the generated StorageClass are.

docs.title: StorageBackup, StorageBackupPolicy, and PersistentVolumeOps
docs.text: 26.3 property 26.4 property Notes StorageBackup.spec.clusterName spec.clusterRef StorageBackup.spec.pvcRef Removed The kind is discovered from the store, not authored. StorageBackup flat status fields status.backup and status.source The copy and the volume it was taken from. BackupPolicy.spec.clusterName StorageBackupPolicy.spec.clusterRef BackupPolicy.status.attachedLvols StorageBackupPolicy.status.attachedClaims VolumeMigration.spec.pvName PersistentVolumeOps.spec.persistentVolumeName VolumeMigration.spec.targetNodeUUID PersistentVolumeOps.spec.migrate.targetNodeRef Names a StorageNode object, not a UUID. VolumeMigration phase Completed PersistentVolumeOps phase Succeeded

docs.title: ControlPlane
docs.text: 26.3 property 26.4 property Notes spec.image spec.source.local.image spec.source.managed names a remote control plane instead. phase Ready phase Available Degraded and Unavailable are added.

docs.title: StorageClass Parameters and Claim Annotations
docs.text:
The QoS keys are renamed outside the CRD schemas as well. Every generation is read, because the parameters of a StorageClass cannot be changed after it is created, so a class an older release generated keeps working.

26.3 parameter 26.4 parameter 26.4 claim annotation qos_rw_iops max_iops storage.simplyblock.io/max-iops qos_rw_mbytes max_mbytes_per_sec storage.simplyblock.io/max-mbytes-per-sec qos_r_mbytes max_read_mbytes_per_sec storage.simplyblock.io/max-read-mbytes-per-sec qos_w_mbytes max_write_mbytes_per_sec storage.simplyblock.io/max-write-mbytes-per-sec

A StorageClass is assigned to a storage pool by three labels, storage.simplyblock.io/namespace, storage.simplyblock.io/cluster, and storage.simplyblock.io/pool, instead of being named after the pool. A pool may have any number of classes. The parameter dhchap_node_label is renamed to dhchap_node_selector, and the node label it names changes from simplyblock.io/pool.<namespace>.<cluster>.<pool> to storage.simplyblock.io/storage-pool.<pool-uuid>.
